newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech builder sees 1997 profit up.
newsitem.headline: Czech builder sees 1997 profit up.

text.p: Czech builder Metrostav a.s. said on Friday it saw its 1997 net profit rising to 136 million crowns from last year's audited net of 94 million.

Speaking at a news conference, Metrostav Finance Director Zdenek Sinovsky also said the board would propose to pay out a "slightly lower" dividend on 1996 earnings than 1995's gross dividend of 70 crowns.
"Net profit should reach 136 million crowns," said Sinovsky.
He added that the company was planning for turnover of 6.4 billion crowns this year after 4.9 billion in 1996.
Metrostav was created as a building firm specialising in tunnel and underground construction, but it has started diversifying its activities.
The director told reporters that Metrostav was planning to expand its equity capital to one billion crowns from the current 658 million by the end of the century.
Metrostav shares are traded on the main market of the Prague Stock Exchange.
